1 سَاعَ , aor. يَسِيعُ, inf. n. سَيْعٌ and سُيُوعٌ, It (water, and the سَرَاب [or mirage],) ran, and was in a state of commotion, upon the surface of the ground; (S, O, K;) as also ↓ انساع : (S:) or the latter, said of water, it ran upon the surface of the ground; as also ↓ تسيّع : and ↓ انساع , said of a thing in a congealed or solid state, signifies also it melted; became fluid, or liquid. (TA.) ―
-b2- سَاعَتِ الإِبِلُ, (Sh, K,) aor. as above, inf. n. سَيْعٌ, (Sh,) The camels were left to themselves, without a pastor; (Sh, K;) as also ساعت having تَسُوعُ for its aor. and سَوْعٌ for its inf. n. (Sh, S * and K * in art. سوع.) ―
-b3- And سَاعَ الشَّىْءَ, aor. as above, The thing became left, or neglected, or lost; or it perished. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
